findings.evidence: The only finite-marginal path-law lemma added is `ExchangeableLaw.map_prefixProj_perm` at lines 84-87; the existing process API has the broader `Exchangeable.blockLaw_eq_prefixLaw_of_injective` at `Contractability.lean:80-83`, and the roadmap calls out finite selections/extension at `README.md:257-261`.
findings.fix: Add a public theorem such as `ExchangeableLaw.map_prefixProj_of_injective (k : Fin n → ℕ) (hk : Function.Injective k) : ρ.map (fun x => fun i : Fin n => x (k i)) = ρ.map (prefixProj α n)`, proved by extending `fun i => i.val` and `k` to a permutation and using `map_permReindex_prefixProj`.
findings.issue: `ExchangeableLaw.map_prefixProj_perm` only handles permutations of the first `n` coordinates, so the path-law API cannot state that an exchangeable law has the same marginal along an arbitrary injective finite selection `k : Fin n → ℕ`.

summary: The new predicate has the basic map and process/path-law bridges, but its finite-dimensional API is too narrow for the path-space use case. Users still lack the path-law analogue of the existing arbitrary injective finite-selection marginal lemma.
